title: Sharps and flats
summary: Black keys borrow their names from the white keys next to them.

steps.title: Sharp means up, flat means down
steps.body:
A black key takes its name from a white key beside it.

- **Sharp** (♯) means one key to the right, a little higher.
- **Flat** (♭) means one key to the left, a little lower.

The black key just right of C is **C sharp**, written C♯.

steps.title: The sharp names
steps.body: Read from the left: C♯, D♯, F♯, G♯ and A♯. Each one is the key just right of the white key it is named after.

steps.title: Flats work the other way
steps.body: The same black keys can also be named from the white key on their right. The black key just left of B is **B flat**, written B♭.

steps.title: The flat names
steps.body: The same five keys, now read as flats: D♭, E♭, G♭, A♭ and B♭.

items.prompt: Play F#: find F, then go one key to the right.
Play Bb: find B, then go one key to the left.

steps.title: Black keys only
steps.body: Play only the black keys for a while, in any order. It always sounds good, because the five black keys make a scale you will meet in a later unit. Watch the names come up as you play.

items.prompt: What is the sharp name of this key?
What is the flat name of this key?
